born.why: This code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding high-risk items and enforcing higher benefit thresholds as health (n1) decreases, switching to a conservative 'a4' stance near critical levels while maintaining aggressive 'a1' acquisition only when the net gain is substantial and health is safe.

This code prioritizes survival by refusing any item that increases health risk (`n1`), accepts healing items, and follows the agent's default choice for neutral items to maintain behavioral consistency without harming health.

The code shifts from reactive to proactive risk management by lowering thresholds for safety choices ('a1') based on both immediate danger (n1) and item threat traits, preventing n1 spikes before they become critical.

The code prioritizes reducing `n1` by taking any item with a positive gain (`x.n1 > x.n2`) and skipping those that increase it, ensuring the agent stays alive as long as possible by keeping health low.

The revised code prioritizes survival by tightening the thresholds for switching to safe options ('a1', 'a2') as n1 rises, ensuring the agent doesn't take unnecessary risks with dangerous items or at high danger levels, while still allowing for reward-seeking behavior when conditions are very safe.

The code prioritizes survival by returning 'a4' (safety) when health (n1) is critical or declining, uses dynamic thresholds based on remaining safety margin to determine if an item's benefit justifies its cost and risk, and restricts approach behavior to high-health states to prevent unnecessary exposure.
